1.sense: The surah opens with the verdict and no introduction at all. Something has taken hold of the reader's attention and kept it, and the something is named second, so the diversion is felt before it is identified.

notes.t: Lahw is amusement that occupies a person and keeps him from what he should be at. The verb alha is causative: not you were amused, but it amused you away from something. What the something is never gets stated, and the silence is part of the accusation.

Takathur is a mutual form of the root k-th-r, much. It does not name having more. It names the two-sided business of having more than somebody else, which cannot be done alone and does not stop on its own.
The Qur'an lists the same competition among the things this life is actually made of, alongside play, adornment and boasting.

links.why: competing in wealth and children, named as what this life consists of
do not let wealth and children divert you, the same verb

2.sense: The counting runs on until the counter is in the ground. The verb is the ordinary word for paying a call on somebody, which makes the grave a place a person stops at rather than a place he stays.

notes.t: Zara is to visit, and a visitor by definition leaves again. The whole doctrine of the resurrection is carried inside that one verb, and the surah does not stop to argue for it here because the word has already done the work.

Commentators report an occasion in which two clans fell to boasting over their numbers and went out to the graveyard to count their dead into the tally. The report is carried in the commentaries rather than in the Sahih collections, and its chains are discussed.
notes.src: recorded by the commentators including Ibn Kathir; not in the two Sahihs, and the chains are discussed

notes.t: Al-maqabir is a plural, the graveyards, and the address is plural too. The picture is not of one funeral but of a whole population arriving at once.

links.why: behind them is a barrier until the Day they are raised
then He caused him to die and had him put in a grave

3.sense: A word of refusal, and then a fact with no object attached. You are going to know is not followed by what you are going to know, which leaves the sentence open and makes it worse rather than vaguer.

notes.t: Kalla is a hard stop in Arabic, a word that rejects what came before it and clears the ground for what follows. It belongs almost entirely to the Makkan surahs, and almost always to people who were certain of themselves.
The object of talamun is deliberately left out. The rhetoricians treat this omission as a device, and its effect is to let each hearer supply the thing he would least like to be told.
The Qur'an ends a warning elsewhere with the same open construction, and there the diverting is named with the same root that opened this surah.

links.why: leave them to eat and be diverted by hope, for they are going to know
and you will certainly know its news after a time

4.sense: The same sentence a second time with one word added in front of it. Nothing new is said, and the repetition is itself the message: the warning is not being explained, it is being pressed.

notes.t: Whether this is one warning said twice for weight or two separate occasions of knowing is an old difference. Those who take it as two name the grave first and the resurrection second, so the sentence is not repeated but rescheduled.
notes.src: at-Tabari records both readings; those who read two occasions name the grave and then the raising

notes.t: Thumma normally opens a gap between two things. Placing it between two identical sentences makes the second one land as a second event rather than as an echo of the first.
An-Naba doubles the same two words in the same order and to the same effect, which shows the construction is a form rather than an accident of this surah.

links.why: the identical doubling in another Makkan warning
every announcement has its settled time, and you are going to know

5.sense: A conditional sentence with its second half missing. If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, and then nothing. The Arabic simply stops, and the reader is left holding the unfinished part of it.

notes.t: The grammarians call the missing half the answer of law, and dropping it here is deliberate. Whatever would have followed, you would not be living like this, is either too large or too obvious to say, so it is not said.

Ilm al-yaqin is the first of three grades the Qur'an works with. Knowledge of certainty is what a person has from being told by someone who does not lie. It is real knowledge, and it is not yet sight.
The third grade, haqq al-yaqin, the truth of certainty, is named in two other places, so the surah is using a scale the Book set up elsewhere.

links.why: the third grade named, the very truth of certainty
and indeed it is the truth of certainty

6.sense: The construction swears the thing twice over, with an emphatic lam in front of the verb and a heavy nun on the end of it. Seeing is promised rather than described, and the surah is still not saying when.

notes.t: A canonical reading turns the verb passive, la-turawunna, you will surely be shown it, which moves the act from the eye to whoever brings the sight about. The consonantal text carries both.
notes.src: al-Kisa'i is transmitted with the passive; Hafs and the majority read the active

notes.t: Al-jahim is from a root for a fire kindled until it stares back. The Arabs used jahmah of a fire whose flames have grown and taken hold of what they are burning.
The Qur'an says elsewhere that the blaze is brought into plain view for anyone with eyes on that Day, which is this promise stated from the other side.

links.why: the blaze brought out into view for whoever sees
there is not one of you but will come to it

7.sense: The same promise a second time, raised a grade. The first said you will see it. This one says what kind of seeing, and the phrase moves the matter out of the ear and into the eye.

notes.t: Ayn is the eye and also the very thing itself. Ayn al-yaqin therefore says eyewitness certainty and certainty itself at the same time, and both senses sit in the phrase without either one crowding the other out.
Verse five said you do not have the first grade of certainty. This verse says you will be given the second whether you want it or not, and thumma keeps the two apart so the upgrade is felt as a step.
Ibrahim asked to be shown rather than told, and was answered, and the reason he gave was that his heart should be settled, which is the same distinction this verse is drawing.

links.why: asking to see what he already believed, so his heart would settle
then they will be the ones entering the blaze

8.sense: The surah ends by turning the ordinary comforts of a life into items on a list of questions. Not the crimes, and not the wealth in the abstract, but the enjoyment of it, which is the part nobody thinks to keep an account of.

notes.t: The Prophet ﷺ went out in hunger with Abu Bakr and Umar and they were given ripe dates, water and meat at an Ansari's house, and he ﷺ told them they would be asked about that delight on the Day of Resurrection. The delight he pointed at was a meal, not a fortune.
notes.src: Muslim 2038, the report of Abu Hurayra on the dates and the cold water

notes.t: The Prophet ﷺ recited this surah and said that the son of Adam claims my wealth, my wealth, while he owns of it only what he ate and used up, what he wore and wore out, and what he gave away and sent on ahead.
An-naim is definite and singular, the delight, not a list of luxuries. It names the whole condition of being comfortable, so shade, water, health and safety are inside it and not exceptions to it.

links.why: the hearing, the sight and the heart, every one of them questioned
if you counted the favours of Allah you could not number them
